rejected.title: Reporting findings
card: A scientific report or poster presents what was done, what was found and what the findings mean. Readers should be able to follow it without the author there.
Use correct scientific terms and symbols. Write units with every measured value, such as 25.0 mL or 0.100 mol L⁻¹. A number without a unit is incomplete.
Show data clearly. In a graph, put the independent variable on the horizontal axis and the dependent variable on the vertical axis. Label both axes with quantity and unit.
Link the conclusion to the data. State what the results show for the aim, and what they imply. Claims must not go beyond what the evidence supports.
rejected.remember: A good report uses correct terms and units, shows data clearly, and draws conclusions that the data supports.

a.q: A student graphs the volume of gas produced against time. Which presentation follows scientific conventions?
opts: Time on the x-axis, volume on the y-axis, both with units
Volume on the x-axis, time on the y-axis, units in the title
Time on the x-axis, volume on the y-axis, no units shown
Both axes labelled with units, but in a random order
a.why: Time is the independent variable, so it goes on the horizontal axis, and the measured volume goes on the vertical axis. Each axis needs its quantity and unit. Putting units only in the title leaves the axes incomplete.
a.clue: Which variable did the student choose, and which did they measure?

b.q: Priya runs one reaction three times with a catalyst and three times without, keeping all other conditions the same. The catalysed trials are faster. Which conclusion is best supported for her report?
opts: The catalyst increased the rate under the conditions tested
The catalyst will increase the rate of every reaction
The catalyst is proven to be the best one available
The results cannot show whether the catalyst had an effect
b.why: The conclusion should match the evidence: one catalyst, one reaction, the conditions tested. Claiming every reaction or the best catalyst goes beyond the data. Saying the results show nothing ignores that she compared trials with and without the catalyst while keeping everything else the same.
b.clue: What did the data actually test, and how far can the claim reach?

Volume on the x-axis, time on the y-axis, units in the title
Time on the x-axis, volume on the y-axis, no units shown
Both axes labelled with units, but in a random order
a.why: Time is the independent variable, so it goes on the horizontal axis, and the measured volume goes on the vertical axis. Each axis needs its quantity and unit. Putting units only in the title leaves the axes incomplete.
a.clue: Which variable did the student choose, and which did they measure?

b.q: Priya runs one reaction three times with a catalyst and three times without, at one temperature, keeping all else the same. The catalysed trials are faster. Which conclusion is best supported for her report?
opts: This catalyst sped up this reaction at that one temperature
This catalyst speeds up all reactions at every temperature
This catalyst is the best one for this reaction at any heat
This catalyst sped up this reaction in only some conditions
b.why: The evidence covers one catalyst, one reaction and one temperature, so the claim should reach only as far as those conditions. Claiming all reactions or every temperature goes beyond the data. Saying it worked only in some conditions is not supported either, as she tested one set of conditions and the catalysed trials were faster.
b.clue: What did the data actually test, and how far can the claim reach?
